Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verses 1–4:

(p-5024) Surat As-Saffat

It was named after the phrase in its opening verse, which describes the angels with attributes that negate their divinity from the aspects that might suggest it. Thereby the divinity of those below them is also negated, which indicates the Oneness of God, and this is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. Said by al-Mahayimi.

It is Meccan by consensus, and its number of verses is one hundred and eighty-two.

Al-Nasa'i narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to instruct us to be brief, and he would lead us in prayer with As-Saffat."

Ibn Kathir said: al-Nasa'i alone narrated it.

(p-5025) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[1–4] ﴿By those who line up in ranks﴾ ﴿and those who drive away with a driving﴾ ﴿and those who recite the reminder﴾ ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾.

The Exalted opened this surah with an oath by some of His creations, to show the greatness of their station and the magnitude of their benefits, and to draw attention to reflecting upon their attributes and what their characteristics entail. (Al-Saffat) is the plural of saffah, meaning a group lined up in rows, or a company lined up.

So in meaning it is a plural of a plural, or it takes the feminine form of its singular, considering it a being and a soul. The intended meaning of "al-saffat" is the angels, because they stand in rows in the station of servitude to the Owner of the dominion, from His saying: ﴿And indeed, we are those who line up﴾ [37:165], or because they spread their wings in the air, standing and awaiting the command of God, the Exalted. And "al-zajirat" means those who restrain people from sins by inspiring good, from (zajr), meaning prohibition and forbidding, or those who drive the celestial and terrestrial bodies by the arrangement that they were commanded, from (zajr) meaning driving and urging. "Al-talayat" means His signs, the Exalted's, upon His prophets, peace be upon them.

It was also said: "al-saffat" are the birds, from His saying: ﴿And the birds in ranks﴾ [24:41]. "Al-zajirat" is everything that restrains from the disobedience of God. "Al-talayat" is everyone who recites the Book of God.

Or they are the scholars who line up their feet in worship, who restrain from disbelief and wickedness with proofs and advice, who recite the signs and laws of God.

Or they are the warriors who line up in jihad, and who drive the horses or the enemy, who recite the remembrance of God, the battle with the enemy not preoccupying them from it. Other than this has been mentioned (p-5026), of what the wording includes and does not reject. In sum, the conjunction is either due to difference in the entities or in the attributes. Preferring the fa' over the waw is for the purpose of sequence and gradation, forward or reverse: as for the first, it is by giving priority to the more important then the more important; as for the second, it is ascending to the higher.

"Saffan" and "zajran" are emphatic verbal nouns (masdar), and likewise "dhikran," though it may also be permissible for it to be an object. Al-Nasir said: In this verse there is evidence for the position of Sibawayh and al-Khalil regarding such examples as: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ [92:1] ﴿and by the day when it displays itself﴾ [92:2], for they both say that the second waw and what follows it are conjunctions (atf). Others hold that they are particles of oath. So the occurrence of fa' in this verse in place of waw has the same meaning, except that what fa' adds of sequence is clear evidence that the waw occurring in this kind of context is for conjunction, not for oath. End.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, your God is One﴾ [37:4], it is the answer to the oath. In emphasizing the sworn matter by placing the oath first and reinforcing the sentence, there is attention to it through establishing the truth in it, which is Oneness, and a preparation for what follows of the proof that speaks to it, namely His, the Exalted's, saying:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[5] ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts.﴾

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts.﴾ Their existence and their orderly arrangement in this wondrous pattern are among the clearest proofs of the existence of the Maker (al-sani'), His knowledge and His power, and the most just testimonies to His oneness. That is: the Owner of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them of existing things, and their Nurturer (murabbi), and the One who brings them to their perfections. By "the easts" is meant the rising-points of the sun (mashariq al-shams). The repetition of the word "Lord" here is for the sake of making the traces of lordship (rububiyyah) most evident in them and renewed every day. For the sun has three hundred and sixty rising-points: it rises each day from one of them, and according to them the setting-points (maghārib) vary, and it sets each day at one of its setting-points. As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ [al-Rahman: 17], these are the two risings of summer and winter and their two settings. This was reported from Abu al-Su'ud.

(p-5027) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6] ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars﴾.

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven﴾, i.e., the nearest direction above the sphere of the earth. ﴿With an adornment﴾, i.e., a wondrous and marvelous one; ﴿of the stars﴾ is in the genitive case (bi-l-jarr), as a substitution (badal) for "adornment." It was also read with the construct form (idafa), either as an explanatory genitive (idafa bayaniyya), or in the sense of "that with which it [the heaven] is adorned," which is its light. The intended meaning of adornment is adornment in the eye of the beholder, for the stars appear to observers as though they were shining jewels.

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿And as a protection from every rebellious devil.﴾

﴿And as a protection from every rebellious devil.﴾ That is: one who has come out of obedience. He (God) pelts him with its meteors, so that he may not stretch himself to eavesdrop on the Heavens from their direction. And: {Protection} (ḥifẓan) is either in the accusative by an implied verb of its own; that is: "We protected them, a protection," or by its being coordinated with {adornment} (zīnah) in meaning; that is: "We made the stars an adornment and a protection for the heaven," or as an object of purpose (al-mafʿūl li-ajlihi) with the addition of the conjunction "wa" (and), the governing element of which is: {We adorned} (zayyannā).

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[8] ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly, and they are pelted from every side.﴾

﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ is read with both the light and the heavy (shaddah) forms of the verb. Its original form is (yastami'un), meaning they seek to hear. The pronoun refers to every devil, since the term is equivalent in meaning to the devils. The clause is a new, independent sentence explaining the condition of those who try to eavesdrop: that they are unable to hear the speech of the angels, and so on. Alternatively, it is a causal clause giving the reason for the guarding; that is, so that they do not hear. The lam was then deleted, followed by (an), and its governing effect was nullified. They considered this weak, because it entails the combination of two deletions, which is objectionable, as they mentioned regarding His words: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [al-Nisa: 176], meaning lest (p-5028) you go astray. It may be said that the objection to deleting two elements applies only where it disrupts the coherence of the speech. As for estimating an element that has parallels, and whose basis is the analysis of a meaning that the wording does not reject, there is no justification for bias in rejecting it merely because the Kufans, for example, or others, held that view. The evidence of meaning is more just than the rule of grammatical principles and their arbitration.

﴿And they are pelted﴾, meaning they are struck with projectiles, ﴿from every side﴾, meaning from all the sides of the sky, whenever they intend to ascend toward it.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿Repelled, and for them is a punishment perpetual.﴾

﴿Repelled﴾ meaning: for repulsion, and it is expulsion (al-dukhur, "expulsion"). ﴿And for them is a punishment perpetual﴾ meaning: severe, not ceasing.

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

[10] ﴿Except one who snatches a snatch, so he is pursued by a piercing flame.﴾

﴿Except one who snatches a snatch﴾, meaning: steals a word. ﴿So he is pursued by a flame﴾, meaning: a fiery spark that falls from the sky overtakes him. ﴿Piercing﴾, meaning: shining, as if it pierces the atmosphere with its light.

Note:

The exegetes mention that the devils used to ascend close to the heaven, and perhaps they would hear the speech of the angels and thereby learn of the unseen matters that were to occur, and they would inform people of them, giving the impression that they knew the unseen. So God, the Exalted, prevented them from ascending near the heaven by these meteors, for He throws them with them and burns them.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, when the devil wants to eavesdrop, a piercing flame comes to him and burns him. For this reason, He, majestic is His majesty, said: ﴿They cannot listen to the exalted assembly﴾ [al-Saffat: 8], meaning: so that they do not reach the exalted assembly, which is the heavens and the angels in them, when they speak of what God, the Exalted, reveals of His law and decree (p-5029); as reports have come about this in the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they say: "What did your Lord say?" They say: "The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great"﴾ [Saba: 23]. End of quote.

Some astronomers have said: Just as the Throne is the dwelling of the unseen spirits — as its explanation has previously been given in the verse ﴿Then He established Himself upon the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf: 54] in al-A'raf — likewise the other planets are inhabited along with animals and creatures by spirits, some of them righteous (the angel) and some of them wicked (the devil). Likewise this earth of ours contains angels and devils that we do not see: ﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them﴾ [al-A'raf: 27].

It is not hidden that non-perception does not indicate non-existence; so our failure to perceive these spirits does not indicate that they do not exist, just as the ancients' lack of knowledge of microbes and electricity, whose great effects are now observed, did not indicate that they did not exist in the world at that time. Denying a thing because of one's ignorance of it or failure to find it is clear folly. Moreover, the matter of summoning spirits now gives us the greatest proof of the existence of spirits on this earth that we do not see and do not perceive.

God, the Exalted, has decreed that animals on this earth, if they leave it for a place where air ceases and breathing stops, die immediately. Likewise He has decreed that the wicked spirits on our earth, when they wish to ascend to the heaven and mingle with the spirits in the other planets, a meteor from these planets, or from elsewhere, swoops down upon them before they leave the earth's atmosphere, burns them and destroys them by corrupting their composition and substance, so that no connection occurs between this and that, nor any gaining of knowledge of the secrets of the other worlds. As for these meteors that fall: if they originate from burning bodies, they are burning; and if they originate from non-burning bodies, they catch fire afterwards because of their great speed and their friction with the gases through which they pass in this atmosphere of ours. Perhaps in the substance of the devils there is something that draws them to these meteors and unites with them, just as chemical elements attract one another.

An example of this is the element sodium, which attracts oxygen from water and decomposes it. We do not say that all meteors fall for this reason; rather, some fall for other reasons, such as the attraction of some celestial bodies to them, and some fall to destroy the devils, as we have explained here. The devils are created from gaseous substances that were burning: ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of the scorching wind﴾ [al-Hijr: 27]. The meaning of "the lowest heaven" in this verse is the space surrounding us and near us; that is, this atmosphere that we observe and in which all the worlds are. As for what lies beyond it, of the distant expanses which we cannot reach with our eyes or with our telescopes, it is pure void containing nothing. The word "heaven" has many meanings, all of which return to the sense of elevation, and it is interpreted in each context according to what fits it.

Then he said: Every matter that the Qur'an has brought is true; there is nothing in natural science that contradicts it, because it is truly the revelation of God, and truth is not contradicted by truth: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is a witness over all things?﴾ [Fussilat: 53]

He also said: Astronomers now believe that most meteors arise from comets, and it is possible that some of them arise from some extinguished suns, or still-burning remnants, or from the volcanoes of some planets, or from what has not yet been extinguished of the planets. And when we know that comets and planets are all derived from suns, the source of all meteors would be the suns or the stars.

(He said): This conveys to us the meaning of this verse. End of his words.

A parallel to this verse is His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils, and prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 5]. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We have certainly placed in the heaven constellations and adorned them for the observers﴾ [al-Hijr: 16], ﴿and guarded them from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17], ﴿except one who eavesdrops, so he is pursued by a clear flame﴾ [al-Hijr: 18] (p-5031). And His, glorified is He, reporting about the jinn: ﴿And we touched the heaven and found it filled with a severe guard and flames﴾ [al-Jinn: 8], ﴿and we used to sit in it on seats for listening; but whoever listens now finds for himself a watching flame﴾ [al-Jinn: 9].

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿So ask them: are they a stronger creation, or those We have created? Indeed We created them from sticky clay.﴾

﴿So ask them﴾, i.e., ask the polytheists of Makkah: ﴿Are they a stronger creation?﴾, i.e., stronger in makeup and firmer in structure, ﴿or those We have created?﴾, i.e., of the heavens, the earth and the mountains, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you a stronger creation or is the sky? ...﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27], to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57]. In their being compelled to answer by the smallness and insignificance of their creation compared with what has been mentioned, there is an acknowledgment that nothing is beyond Him after this, such as the matter of the Resurrection and other things, and to this the Exalted's saying refers: ﴿Indeed We created them from sticky clay﴾, i.e., clay that is viscous and weak, having no strength in it.

Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[12] ﴿Nay, you wonder, while they mock﴾.

﴿Nay, you wonder﴾, that is: at their denial of the Resurrection, after they have been compelled to acknowledge the evidence that establishes it. ﴿While they mock﴾, that is: at the affirmation of the matter of the Resurrection and the argument presented for it.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[13] ﴿And when they are reminded, they do not remember.﴾

﴿And when they are reminded﴾ meaning: with that which confirms it, or they are admonished and warned against opposition. ﴿They do not remember﴾ meaning: they do not heed what it requires, due to their obstinacy and stubbornness; or they do not fear and are not admonished.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 14:

(p-5032) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿And when they see a sign, they mock.﴾

﴿And when they see a sign﴾, i.e., a proof and an argument for its truth, from the signs of the created beings within themselves or in the horizons, ﴿they mock﴾, i.e., they exaggerate in ridicule, instead of taking heed (i'tibar), reflecting (tadabbur), and contemplating (tafakkur).

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[15] ﴿And they say, "This is nothing but evident magic."﴾

﴿And they say, "This is...﴾ i.e., the claim to what has been mentioned, the argument for it, the proclaiming of its matter, and the contending over it: ﴿...nothing but evident magic.﴾

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[16–18] ﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? And our forefathers of old?﴾ ﴿Say: "Yes, and you will be humbled."﴾

﴿When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?﴾ ﴿And our forefathers of old?﴾ ﴿Say﴾ — i.e., as a rebuke to them: ﴿Yes﴾ — i.e., you will be resurrected; ﴿and you will be humbled﴾ — i.e., abased, with no argument from you that could repel it, and no power.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 23:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[23] ﴿Other than Allah, so lead them to the path of Hellfire.﴾

﴿Other than Allah﴾ means: from the idols and others, as an increase in their humiliation and their shame. ﴿So lead them to the path of Hellfire﴾ means: inform them of its way so that they may take it. The use of the expressions "guidance" (hidayah) and "path" (sirat) is for mockery of them.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[24] ﴿And stop them, indeed they are to be questioned.﴾

﴿Stop them﴾ means: detain them at the place of standing (al-mawqif). ﴿Indeed they are to be questioned﴾ means: about their beliefs and their deeds.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[25] ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not help one another?﴾

﴿What is wrong with you that you do not help one another?﴾ That is, none of you helps another, though your custom in the former life was mutual support. This is a rebuke and a reproach to them.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[26] ﴿Nay, today they will be submitting [to one another].﴾

﴿Nay, today they will be submitting﴾, i.e., surrendering in compliance, forsaken.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[27–28] ﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other.﴾ ﴿They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right."﴾ [al-Saffat: 28]

﴿And they will turn to one another, questioning each other.﴾ ﴿They will say, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right."﴾ [al-Saffat: 28] That is, from the side of compulsion and domination, meaning you used to force us into what you were calling us to, as in the verse: ﴿Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, [it was] the plotting of night and day, when you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him."﴾ [Saba': 33]. It was also said: from the side of oaths and swearing. It was also said: from the direction of goodness and the side of truth, from *al-yaman* (اليمن, "the blessed side, good fortune"), the opposite of *al-shu'm* (الشؤم, "ill omen"). That is, you deceived us and tricked us into thinking that what you were upon was a blessed matter in which there was good and success. So where is its fulfilment, when what has befallen has befallen?

﴿And they say, "Shall we abandon our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ That is: for the speech of one who says, with imaginative premises, that he is mad. So He refuted them by saying that he did not bring speech that was imagined.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verses 46–47:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[46, 47] ﴿White, delicious to the drinkers﴾ ﴿There is no harm in it, nor are they intoxicated by it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47].

﴿White, delicious to the drinkers﴾ ﴿There is no harm in it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47]: that is, it does not seize the intellect (ghawl), nor is there any corruption of the sort found in the wine of this world. ﴿Nor are they intoxicated by it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47]: that is, their intellects do not depart.

(p-5037) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[48, 49] ﴿And with them will be those of restrained gaze, with beautiful eyes﴾ ﴿as if they were eggs well-guarded﴾ [al-Saffat: 49].

﴿And with them will be those of restrained gaze﴾, i.e., restricted to their husbands, or whitened (mubayyadat) by it, likening them to a garment that is kept (maqsur), which is the one that is whitened (al-muhawwar). ﴿With beautiful eyes﴾, i.e., large-eyed. ﴿As if they were eggs well-guarded﴾ [al-Saffat: 49], i.e., ostrich eggs in their clearness, concealed and undisturbed by dust. Al-Shihab said: This is in accordance with the custom of the Arabs in comparing women to them, and it was specified to ostrich eggs because of its clearness, and because it is more pleasing in appearance than the rest of it, and because it lays its eggs in the open desert and keeps its eggs far from being touched. Hence the Arabs said of women: "white ones of the howdahs" (baydat al-khudur). And because its whiteness is mixed with a slight yellowness along with a sheen, as in pearls, and this is a very praiseworthy colour, since pure whiteness is not praiseworthy; it is only praised when it is mixed with a slight redness in men and a slight yellowness in women. End of quote.

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Abbas that he meant by the well-guarded eggs: "pearls."

[48, 49] ﴿And with them will be those of restrained gaze, with beautiful eyes﴾ ﴿as if they were eggs well-guarded﴾ [al-Saffat: 49].

﴿And with them will be those of restrained gaze﴾, i.e., restricted to their husbands, or whitened (mubayyadat) by it, likening them to a garment that is kept (maqsur), which is the one that is whitened (al-muhawwar). ﴿With beautiful eyes﴾, i.e., large-eyed. ﴿As if they were eggs well-guarded﴾ [al-Saffat: 49], i.e., ostrich eggs in their clearness, concealed and undisturbed by dust. Al-Shihab said: This is in accordance with the custom of the Arabs in comparing women to them, and it was specified to ostrich eggs because of its clearness, and because it is more pleasing in appearance than the rest of it, and because it lays its eggs in the open desert and keeps its eggs far from being touched. Hence the Arabs said of women: "white ones of the howdahs" (baydat al-khudur). And because its whiteness is mixed with a slight yellowness along with a sheen, as in pearls, and this is a very praiseworthy colour, since pure whiteness is not praiseworthy; it is only praised when it is mixed with a slight redness in men and a slight yellowness in women. The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[63–65] ﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs forth from the root of Hellfire.﴾ [al-Saffat: 64] ﴿Its spathes are like the heads of devils.﴾ [al-Saffat: 65]

﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial﴾, i.e., a tribulation and a punishment, ﴿for the wrongdoers﴾. ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs forth from the root of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 64]. ﴿Its spathes﴾ [al-Saffat: 65], i.e., its fruit-bearing, ﴿are like the heads of devils﴾ [al-Saffat: 65], i.e., like what is imagined and conceived of the ugliness of the heads of devils. So it is ugly in its root, its fruit, its appearance, and its touch.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It was compared to the heads of devils to indicate its extreme repulsiveness and the ugliness of its appearance, because the devil is hateful and considered repugnant in the natures of people, since they believe that he is pure evil with no good mixed into him. So they say of a person of ugly form: "as if he were the face of a devil" and "as if he were the head of a devil." When artists depict him, they bring his image in the most hideous and frightful form that can be imagined. Likewise, they believed that the angel is pure good with no evil in him, so they compared beautiful forms to him. God, Exalted, said: ﴿This is no mortal; this is none but a noble angel﴾ [Yusuf: 31]. This is an imaginative comparison (*takhyili*). End of quote. That is, it is for a matter fixed in the imagination.

By this, the objection is dispelled that it is a comparison to something unknown. For it is not required that the thing be known in external reality; it is sufficient that it be fixed in the mind and imagination (p-5041). Do you not see that Imru' al-Qays, who was the king of poets, says:

*And sharpened, blue, like the fangs of ghouls* (*ghul*, a kind of demon)

He had not seen the ghoul, and the ghoul is a type of devil; for it is imprinted in everyone's imagination in a hideous form, even though it is capable of taking various shapes.

The discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[66] ﴿Indeed, they will eat from it, and fill their bellies with it.﴾

﴿Indeed, they will eat from it﴾, i.e., from its spathe (ṭalʿ): ﴿and fill their bellies with it﴾, i.e., due to the overpowering of hunger, or the compulsion to eat it.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[67] ﴿Then indeed they will have on top of it a mixture of boiling water.﴾

﴿Then indeed they will have on top of it a mixture of boiling water﴾ means: a drink like pus (al-sadid) or ghassaq (al-ghassaq), mixed with water that has reached the utmost heat, which cuts up their intestines.

The discussion of the verse: His saying, may He be exalted:

[68] ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire.﴾

﴿Then indeed their return﴾ means their destination; ﴿is to the Hellfire﴾ means to its levels, or to the Fire itself, from which there is no escape for them and no way out, however they turn. Ibn Kathir said: That is, then indeed their return after this separation is to a fire that blazes and a blaze that flares up, so at one time in this and at another time in that, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, intensely hot﴾ [al-Rahman: 44]. Qatadah recited this verse at this point, in this manner. It is a good and strong interpretation. End of quote.

Among the subtle allusions regarding this verse is what al-Qashani said, and his words are: ﴿It is a tree that springs forth from the root of the Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 64]. It is the tree of the wicked, veiled soul, rooted in the depths of Hell, its branches spreading through its ugly and terrifying levels, its fruits from the vices and evil qualities, as if they were, from the extreme of ugliness, deformity and foulness, in their repulsiveness: ﴿like the heads of devils﴾ [al-Saffat: 65], that is, from it arise the destructive motives and the ruinous impulses that drive one to ugly deeds and wicked actions. Those are the roots of satanic nature and the beginnings of evil and corruption, so they are called the heads of devils. ﴿Indeed they will eat from it﴾ [al-Saffat: 66], drawing strength from it, nourishing themselves and empowering themselves, for the wicked find their nourishment in evils and take pleasure in nothing but them. ﴿Then they will fill their bellies with it﴾ [al-Saffat: 66], with corrupt states and dark qualities, like one filled with anger, spite and envy at the time of their agitation. ﴿Then indeed for them over it is a mixture of scalding water﴾ [al-Saffat: 67], the natural desires, the evil and vile wishes, the love of lowly matters, and the palaces of ruinous evils, which break some of the thirst of the wicked. ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 68], because of the predominance of greed and avidity, through lust, spite, hatred and the like, and the seizure of their motives while the attainment of their objects is impossible. End of quote.

These allusions are among the figurative meanings which the language can bear, since they are not confined to the literal sense. It cannot be said that they are the intended meaning here, given that they are remote from parallel verses of warning. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verses 69–70:

(p-5043) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[69, 70] ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray,﴾ ﴿so they were hastening in their footsteps.﴾ [al-Saffat: 70].

﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray﴾ ﴿so they were hastening in their footsteps﴾ [al-Saffat: 70] is an explanation for why they deserve those torments, by their imitation (taqlid) of their fathers in misguidance. (Al-Ihra'): the very swift hastening, as if they were being driven to hurry along in their footsteps. Al-Razi said: "Had there been no verse in the Qur'an condemning imitation (taqlid) other than this verse, it would have sufficed."

**The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

**[78, 79]** ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 79].

: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾, i.e., We caused to remain for him among the nations after him a good mention (ثَناءً حَسَنًا). The object of (تَرَكْنا) *taraknā* ("We left") is therefore omitted. Alternatively, the object is what Exalted is He relates with His saying: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 79], i.e., that they would greet him with peace until the Day of Resurrection; that is, that they would say this sentence.

Al-Samin said: His saying: ﴿Peace upon Noah﴾ [al-Saffat: 79] is a *mubtada'* (subject) and *khabar* (predicate), and in it there are several possibilities:

The first is that it explains (تَرَكْنا) *taraknā*. The second is that it explains its object, i.e., "We left upon him something, and that thing is this statement." Or there is an implied saying, i.e., "So We said: Peace." Or (تَرَكْنا) *taraknā* is taken to include the meaning of (قُلْنا) *qulnā* ("We said"), or (تَرَكْنا) *taraknā* is given authority over what follows it. It has also been read (سَلامًا) *salāman* in the accusative, in which case it is the direct object of (تَرَكْنا) *taraknā*.

**The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

**[78, 79]** ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾ ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 79].

: ﴿And We left for him among the later generations﴾, i.e., We caused to remain for him among the nations after him a good mention (ثَناءً حَسَنًا). The object of (تَرَكْنا) *taraknā* ("We left") is therefore omitted. Alternatively, the object is what Exalted is He relates with His saying: ﴿Peace upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 79], i.e., that they would greet him with peace until the Day of Resurrection; that is, that they would say this sentence.

It has also been read (سَلامًا) *salāman* in the accusative, in which case it is the direct object of (تَرَكْنا) *taraknā*.

Commentary on the words of God Most High:

[80] ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾

﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ This is a justification for the honour with which he was rewarded: it is a recompense for his good conduct, namely his striving (mujahadah) in raising the word of God and calling to the truth by night and by day, secretly and openly.

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[81] ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants.﴾

﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾: i.e., among those who affirm (al-musaddiqin). The attribution of his excellence (ihsan) to faith (iman) serves to demonstrate the virtue of faith and its distinction, since He praised with it one who is among the great messengers. Thus the intended purpose of the attribute is to praise the attribute itself, not to praise the one it describes, because faith is the foundation of every good that exists, the center of its circle, and the musk of its seal.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[82] ﴿Then We drowned the others.﴾

﴿Then We drowned the others.﴾ That is, of the disbelievers among his people.

Commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[83] ﴿And indeed, among his followers was Abraham.﴾

﴿And indeed, among his followers was Abraham.﴾ That is: among those who supported him, and followed him in faith and in the vigorous call to monotheism (tawhid).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 84:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[84] ﴿When he came to his Lord with a sound heart.﴾

﴿When he came to his Lord with a sound heart.﴾ That is: he turned toward His Oneness with a heart pure of impurities (p-5046), remaining upon the natural disposition (fitrah), sound and free from defects and afflictions, adhering to the covenant of the innate Oneness (tawhid), and disapproving of those who altered and changed it.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[85] ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾

﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship?"﴾ That is: apart from Allah.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[86] ﴿Is it a falsehood, gods other than God that you desire?﴾

﴿Is it a falsehood, gods other than God that you desire?﴾ That is: Do you desire, by way of lying, gods other than God?

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[87] ﴿So what is your assumption about the Lord of the worlds?﴾

﴿So what is your assumption about the Lord of the worlds?﴾ That is: concerning the One who is deserving of worship, by virtue of being the Lord of the worlds, such that you abandoned His worship and associated others with Him. The meaning: no notion or assumption can conceive of anything that would turn one away from worshipping Him, for His deserving to be worshipped is too clear for any trace of doubt to stir concerning it. Thus He rejects their assumption, which lies in the matter of explaining His deserving to be worshipped, and which is what led them to worship other than Him. Or the meaning is: "So what is your assumption about Him? What will He do to you, and how will He punish you, when you have worshipped other than Him?" In either case, the interrogation is one of denial. What is meant by denying the assumption is denying what it entails.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[88] ﴿So he glanced a glance at the stars﴾.

﴿So he glanced a glance at the stars﴾: that is, so that he might show them that he was drawing an inference from them to something, because they were astrologers (munajjimin).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 89:

(p-5047) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[89] ﴿So he said, "Indeed, I am ill."﴾

﴿So he said, "Indeed, I am ill."﴾ That is: sick, unable to go out with you to your festival. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, took this dispensation (tarakhkhusa) so that he might free himself from their false witness (shuhud zur), their reprehensible practices (munkarat), and the various forms of their polytheism (afanin shirkihim), which the public good (al-maslaha) permits. Or he meant that he was sick at heart, likening his distress and sorrow to illness, by way of simile (al-tashbih). Or he meant that he was prepared for death as the sick man is prepared, so it is a metaphor (isti'ara), or a loose figurative usage (majaz mursal).

Al-Zamakhshari said: What Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said is a piece of equivocal speech (mi'radun min al-kalam), and he intended by it that whoever has death at his neck is sick. From this is the proverb: "Safety is enough of an affliction" (kafa bil-salamati da'un). And the verse of Labid:

"I prayed to my Lord earnestly for safety, that it might make me healthy, but when safety came, it was an affliction."

A man died suddenly, and the people gathered around him, saying: "He died while healthy." A Bedouin said:

"Is one healthy whose neck bears death?" End of quotation.

Al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): In the verse is the use of equivocal speech (al-ma'arid) and figurative language for the sake of the public good.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[90] ﴿So they turned away from him, going off in retreat.﴾

﴿So they turned away from him, going off in retreat.﴾ That is: to their place of worship.

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted: [91] ﴿So he turned aside to their gods and said, "Will you not eat?"﴾

﴿So he turned aside to their gods﴾, i.e., he went to them secretly. ﴿And said﴾, i.e., to the idols, mockingly: ﴿"Will you not eat?"﴾

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[92] ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not speak?﴾ ﴿Then he turned upon them, striking them with the right hand.﴾ [al-Saffat: 93] ﴿So they came hastening toward him.﴾ [al-Saffat: 94] ﴿He said, "Do you worship what you carve?"﴾ [al-Saffat: 95] ﴿While Allah created you and what you do.﴾ [al-Saffat: 96].

﴿What is wrong with you that you do not speak?﴾ That is: neither affirming nor negating. ﴿Then he turned upon them﴾ [al-Saffat: 93], that is, he attacked them, ﴿striking them with the right hand﴾ [al-Saffat: 93], that is, the one which is the stronger of the two striking hands, so he broke them. ﴿So they came hastening toward him﴾ [al-Saffat: 94], that is, toward Ibrahim, after they had returned. ﴿Hastening﴾ [al-Saffat: 94], that is, they hurried to rebuke him for what had come from him. Then peace be upon him began to demonstrate to them the corruption of their worship. ﴿He said, "Do you worship what you carve?"﴾ [al-Saffat: 95], that is, from the idols. ﴿While Allah created you and what you do﴾ [al-Saffat: 96], that is, and what you make of the idols, varied in forms and differing in sizes. And when the proof was established against them, they resorted to seizing him by force and coercion.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verses 97–98:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[97, 98] ﴿They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire."﴾ ﴿So they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the most debased.﴾ [al-Saffat: 98].

﴿They said, "Build for him"﴾, i.e., for burning him, ﴿a structure and throw him into the blazing fire.﴾ ﴿So they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the most debased.﴾ [al-Saffat: 98], i.e., the most humiliated, by nullifying their scheme. He made the fire cool and safe for him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verses 97–98:

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[97, 98] ﴿They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire."﴾ ﴿So they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the most debased.﴾ [al-Saffat: 98].

﴿They said, "Build for him"﴾, i.e., for burning him, ﴿a structure and throw him into the blazing fire.﴾ ﴿So they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the most debased.﴾ [al-Saffat: 98], i.e., the most humiliated, by nullifying their scheme. He made the fire cool and safe for him.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[99] ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾

﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ That is: I am emigrating to a land where I may worship my Lord and preserve my religion therein.

Al-Razi said: In this is evidence that a place in which enemies are numerous must be emigrated from, for Abraham, peace be upon him, despite what God Most High had granted him of the greatest kinds of support, when he perceived intense enmity from his people, emigrated. So it is all the more obligatory for others.

As for His words, ﴿He will guide me﴾: that is, to that which contains the welfare of my religion, or to my destination. He stated it definitively because of the precedence of God's promise, since He undertook to guide him; or because whoever is with God, God is with him: "Guard God, and He will guard you."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[100, 101] ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy. [al-Saffat: 101]

﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ That is, a righteous son who will help me in calling to the faith and in obedience. ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ [al-Saffat: 101] That is, one of broad breast, good patience, and forgiving disposition in every matter. Forbearance (hilm) is the head of righteousness and the root of all virtues.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[100, 101] ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy. [al-Saffat: 101]

﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.﴾ That is, a righteous son who will help me in calling to the faith and in obedience. ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.﴾ [al-Saffat: 101] That is, one of broad breast, good patience, and forgiving disposition in every matter. Forbearance (hilm) is the head of righteousness and the root of all virtues.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[102] ﴿So when he reached with him the age of exertion, he said, "O my son, I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, God willing, among the steadfast."﴾

﴿So when he reached with him the age of exertion﴾ means the age at which he is able to exert himself in work and in learning. ﴿He said, "O my son, I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think."﴾ means: I have been commanded in a dream to slaughter you. The visions of the prophets are a revelation, like revelation received while awake. ﴿So see whether you will be patient in carrying out my command regarding the vision and acting upon its apparent meaning.﴾ ﴿He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded."﴾ means: what God commands you to do. If that is a command from Him, then carry it out.

Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: Perhaps he understood from his words that he saw himself slaughtering him as something commanded, or he knew that the visions of the prophets are true, and that such people do not undertake such a thing except by command. He then said: Perhaps the command was in the dream and not while awake, so that their hastening to comply would be more evidence of complete submission and sincerity. End of quotation.

Al-Razi said: The wisdom in consulting the son on this matter is that he informs his son of this event so that he may show him his patience in obeying God. Thus there is comfort of the eye for Ibrahim, as he sees him having reached such a great level of forbearance, and such lofty steadfastness in bearing the most severe hardships. The son also obtains great reward in the Hereafter and fine praise in this world. His words, ﴿You will find me, God willing, among the steadfast﴾ mean: in submitting to the slaughter, or in accepting God's decree.

The discussion of the words of His saying, the Exalted:

[103] ﴿So when they had both submitted, and he had laid him down upon his forehead﴾.

﴿When they had both submitted﴾: i.e., they surrendered and yielded to His command, the Exalted, without delay, and Ibrahim drew the knife.

﴿And he had laid him down upon his forehead﴾: i.e., he threw him down on his side, so that his temple fell upon the ground, and the jabin is one of the two sides of the forehead. Talla (تَلَّ) originally means: he threw him onto the tall (al-tall), which is the heaped-up earth, like: (tariba), i.e., he put him in the dust. Then it became general for every act of throwing down.

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[104, 105] ﴿And We called out to him, "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision."﴾ ﴿Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.﴾ [al-Saffat: 105].

﴿And We called out to him, "O Abraham"﴾ ﴿"you have fulfilled the vision"﴾ [al-Saffat: 105], meaning: do not slaughter him, for you have already realized its fulfillment by exerting your utmost effort in carrying out what it indicated, and by perfect obedience in this arduous matter. You have been granted the reward of compliance, of patience, and of steadfastness. Regarding the answer to (lamma) (when) there are three possibilities, the most evident of which is that it is omitted, i.e., "the angels called out to him" (p-5051), or "their patience became manifest," or "We granted them a generous reward." The second: the answer is ﴿And he laid him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], with the waw being extra; this is the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash. The third: the answer is ﴿And We called out to him﴾, with the waw likewise being extra. ﴿Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good﴾ [al-Saffat: 105], i.e., with kindness, care, the call, revelation, and relief after hardship.

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[104, 105] ﴿And We called out to him, "O Abraham, you have fulfilled the vision."﴾ ﴿Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.﴾ [al-Saffat: 105].

﴿And We called out to him, "O Abraham"﴾ ﴿"you have fulfilled the vision"﴾ [al-Saffat: 105], meaning: do not slaughter him, for you have already realized its fulfillment by exerting your utmost effort in carrying out what it indicated, and by perfect obedience in this arduous matter. You have been granted the reward of compliance, of patience, and of steadfastness. The second: the answer is ﴿And he laid him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], with the waw being extra; this is the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash. The third: the answer is ﴿And We called out to him﴾, with the waw likewise being extra. ﴿Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good﴾ [al-Saffat: 105], i.e., with kindness, care, the call, revelation, and relief after hardship.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 106:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[106] ﴿Indeed, this was a clear trial.﴾

﴿Indeed, this was a clear trial.﴾ That is: the manifest test (al-ikhtibar) by which the sincere one is distinguished from others, indicating that this command was a trial and an examination for Ibrahim (Abraham) in the truthfulness of his friendship (khullah) with God, and in sacrificing the most beloved of the beloved to him and the dearest of the dear to him, in obedience to the command of his Lord, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 107:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[107] ﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.﴾

﴿And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice﴾, i.e., We provided him with that which would be slaughtered as a substitute for him and as a ransom for him, as a favour and a bounty. It has been narrated that when he (peace be upon him) was called, he turned his gaze towards what was around him, and he saw a ram whose horns had become entangled in a tree, and thus what he had seen in the dream, which was intended as an offering to God, was fulfilled through it.

القَوْلُ في تَأْوِيلِ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى:
[ ١٠٨ - ١١٣ ] ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١] ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] ﴿وبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ وعَلى إسْحاقَ ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِما مُحْسِنٌ وظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ مُبِينٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] .
(p-5052) ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] أي: مِثْلَ ما تَرَكْنا عَلى نُوحٍ، كَما تَقَدَّمَ بَيانُهُ وإعْرابُهُ (i'rab: the grammatical analysis of the Arabic words). ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١] ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] ﴿وبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: عَلى إبْراهِيمَ. ﴿وعَلى إسْحاقَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: بِتَكْثِيرِ الذُّرِّيَّةِ وتَسَلْسُلِ النُّبُوَّةِ فِيهِمْ، وجَعْلِهِمْ مُلُوكًا، وإيتائِهِمْ ما لَمْ يُؤْتَ أحَدٌ. ﴿ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِما مُحْسِنٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: في عَمَلِهِ. ﴿وظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: بِالكُفْرِ والمَعاصِي. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: ظاهِرُ الظُّلْمِ.

تَنْبِيهاتٌ:

الأوَّلُ: يَرْوِي المُفَسِّرُونَ هَهُنا في قِصَّةِ الذَّبْحِ رِواياتٍ مُنْكَرَةً لَمْ يَصِحَّ سَنَدُها ولا مَتْنُها، بَلْ ولَمْ تَحْسُنْ، فَهي مُعْضِلَةٌ تَنْتَهِي إلى السُّدِّيِّ وكَعْبٍ. والسُّدِّيُّ حالُهُ مَعْلُومٌ في ضَعْفِ مَرْوِيّاتِهِ، وكَذَلِكَ كَعْبٌ.

قالَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: لَمّا أسْلَمَ كَعْبُ الأحْبارِ في الدَّوْلَةِ العُمَرِيَّةِ، جَعَلَ يُحَدِّثُ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ كُتُبِهِ قَدِيمًا، فَرُبَّما اسْتَمَعَ لَهُ عُمَرُ، فَتَرَخَّصَ النّاسُ في اسْتِماعِ ما عِنْدَهُ عَنْهُ، غَثِّها وسَمِينِها، ولَيْسَ لِهَذِهِ الأُمَّةِ حاجَةٌ إلى حَرْفٍ واحِدٍ مِمّا عِنْدَهُ. انْتَهى.

ولَقَدْ صَدَقَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ، ولِذا نَرى التَّزَيُّدَ عَلى أصْلِ ما قَصَّ في التَّنْزِيلِ مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ لَهُ، إلّا إذا صَحَّ سَنَدُهُ، أوِ اطْمَأنَّ القَلْبُ بِهِ. وقَدْ ولِعَ الخُطَباءُ في دَواوِينِهِمْ بِرِوايَةِ هَذِهِ القِصَّةِ في خُطْبَةِ الأضْحى مِن طُرُقِها الواهِيَةِ عِنْدَ المُحَدِّثِينَ، ويَرَوْنَها ضَرْبَةَ لازِبٍ عَلى ضَعْفِ سَنَدِها، وكَوْنِ مَتْنِها مُنْكَرًا أيْضًا أوْ مَوْضُوعًا. ولَمّا صَنَّفْتُ مَجْمُوعَةَ الخُطَبِ حَذَفْتُ هَذِهِ الرِّوايَةَ مِن خُطْبَةِ الأضْحى كَكُلِّ مَرْوِيٍّ ضَعِيفٍ في فَضائِلِ الشُّهُورِ والأوْقاتِ، واقْتَصَرْتُ عَلى جِيادِ الأخْبارِ والآثارِ، وذَلِكَ مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنا فَلا نُحْصِي ثَناءً عَلَيْهِ.

وأمْثَلُ ما رُوِيَ في هَذا النَّبَأِ مِنَ (p-5053) الآثارِ ما أخْرَجَهُ الإمامُ أحْمَدُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُما مَوْقُوفًا، قالَ: لَمّا أُمِرَ إبْراهِيمُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ بِالمَناسِكِ، عَرَضَ لَهُ الشَّيْطانُ عِنْدَ السَّعْيِ، فَسابَقَهُ فَسَبَقَهُ إبْراهِيمُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ إلى جَمْرَةِ العَقَبَةِ، فَعَرَضَ لَهُ الشَّيْطانُ فَرَماهُ بِسَبْعِ حَصَياتٍ حَتّى ذَهَبَ، ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لَهُ عِنْدَ الجَمْرَةِ الوُسْطى فَرَماهُ بِسَبْعِ حَصَياتٍ، ثُمَّ تَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ، وعَلى إسْماعِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَمِيصٌ أبْيَضُ، فَقالَ لَهُ: يا أبَتِ! إنَّهُ لَيْسَ لِي ثَوْبٌ تُكَفِّنُنِي فِيهِ غَيْرُهُ، فاخْلَعْهُ حَتّى تُكَفِّنَنِي فِيهِ، فَعالَجَهُ لِيُخْلِصَهُ، فَنُودِيَ مِن خَلْفِهِ: أنْ يا إبْراهِيمُ قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيا. فالتَفَتَ إبْراهِيمُ فَإذا بِكَبْشٍ أبْيَضَ أقْرَنَ أعْيَنَ. قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: لَقَدْ رَأيْتُنا نَتَتَبَّعُ ذَلِكَ الضَّرْبَ مِنَ الكِباشِ.

الثّانِي: قالَ السُّيُوطِيُّ في (الإكْلِيلِ): في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ أنَّ رُؤْيا الأنْبِياءِ وحْيٌ، وجَوازُ نَسْخِ الفِعْلِ قَبْلَ التَّمَكُّنِ (naskh: abrogation of a ruling before it is carried out)، وتَقْدِيمُ المَشِيئَةِ في كُلِّ قَوْلٍ، واسْتَدَلَّ بَعْضُهم بِهَذِهِ القِصَّةِ عَلى أنَّ مَن نَذَرَ ذَبْحَ ولَدِهِ، لَزِمَهُ ذَبْحُ شاةٍ.

ثُمَّ قالَ السُّيُوطِيُّ: فُسِّرَ الذِّبْحُ العَظِيمُ في الأحادِيثِ والآثارِ بِكَبْشٍ، فاسْتَدَلَّ بِهِ المالِكِيَّةُ عَلى أنَّ الغَنَمَ في التَّضْحِيَةِ أفْضَلُ مِنَ الإبِلِ. انْتَهى.

الثّالِثُ: اُسْتُدِلَّ بِالآيَةِ عَلى أنَّهُ تَعالى قَدْ يَأْمُرُ بِما لا يُرِيدُ وُقُوعَهُ، كَما ذَكَرَهُ الرّازِيُّ، وذَلِكَ في بابِ الِابْتِلاءِ، أيِ: ابْتِلاءِ المَأْمُورِ في إخْلاصِهِ وصِدْقِهِ، فِيما يَشُقُّ عَلى النَّفْسِ تَحَمُّلُهُ.

الرّابِعُ: يَذْكُرُ كَثِيرٌ الخِلافَ في الذَّبِيحِ. قالَ الإمامُ ابْنُ القَيِّمِ في (زادِ المَعادِ): وإسْماعِيلُ هو الذَّبِيحُ عَلى القَوْلِ الصَّوابِ عِنْدَ عُلَماءِ الصَّحابَةِ والتّابِعِينَ ومَن بَعْدَهُمْ، وأمّا القَوْلُ بِأنَّهُ إسْحاقُ فَباطِلٌ بِأكْثَرَ مِن عِشْرِينَ وجْهًا. وسَمِعْتُ شَيْخَ الإسْلامِ ابْنَ تَيْمِيَةَ قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ رُوحَهُ يَقُولُ: هَذا القَوْلُ إنَّما هو مُتَلَقًّى مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ، مَعَ أنَّهُ باطِلٌ بِنَصِّ كِتابِهِمْ؛ فَإنَّ فِيهِ إنَّ اللَّهَ أمَرَ (p-5054) إبْراهِيمَ أنْ يَذْبَحَ ابْنَهُ (بِكْرَهُ)، وفي لَفْظٍ: (وحِيدَهُ)، ولا يَشُكُّ أهْلُ الكِتابِ مَعَ المُسْلِمِينَ أنَّ إسْماعِيلَ هو بِكْرُ أوْلادِهِ.

والَّذِي غَرَّ أصْحابَ هَذا القَوْلِ أنَّ في التَّوْراةِ الَّتِي بِأيْدِيهِمْ: (اذْبَحِ ابْنَكَ إسْحاقَ).

قالَ: وهَذِهِ الزِّيادَةُ مِن تَحْرِيفِهِمْ وكَذِبِهِمْ؛ لِأنَّها تُناقِضُ قَوْلَهُ: بِكْرَكَ، وحِيدَكَ. ولَكِنَّ يَهُودَ حَسَدَتْ بَنِي إسْماعِيلَ عَلى هَذا الشَّرَفِ، وأحَبُّوا أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمْ، وأنْ يَسُوقُوهُ إلَيْهِمْ، ويَخْتارُوهُ دُونَ العَرَبِ. ويَأْبى اللَّهُ إلّا أنْ يَجْعَلَ فَضْلَهُ لِأهْلِهِ. وكَيْفَ يُسَوَّغُ أنْ يُقالَ إنَّ الذَّبِيحَ إسْحاقُ، واللَّهُ تَعالى قَدْ بَشَّرَ أُمَّ إسْحاقَ بِهِ وبِابْنِهِ يَعْقُوبَ، فَقالَ تَعالى عَنِ المَلائِكَةِ أنَّهم قالُوا لِإبْراهِيمَ لَمّا أتَوْهُ بِالبُشْرى: ﴿لا تَخَفْ إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾ [هود: ٧٠] ﴿وامْرَأتُهُ قائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْناها بِإسْحاقَ ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ [هود: ٧١]. فَمُحالٌ أنْ يُبَشِّرَها بِأنَّهُ يَكُونُ لَها ولَدٌ ثُمَّ يَأْمُرُ بِذَبْحِهِ. ولا رَيْبَ أنَّ يَعْقُوبَ داخِلٌ في البِشارَةِ، فَتَناوُلُ البِشارَةِ لِإسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ في اللَّفْظِ واحِدٌ. وهَذا ظاهِرُ الكَلامِ وسِياقُهُ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: لَوْ كانَ الأمْرُ كَما ذَكَرْتُمُوهُ لَكانَ يَعْقُوبُ مَجْرُورًا عَطْفًا عَلى إسْحاقَ، فَكانَتِ القِراءَةُ: ﴿ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ [هود: ٧١] أيْ: ويَعْقُوبُ مِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ. قِيلَ: لا يَمْنَعُ الرَّفْعُ أنْ يَكُونَ يَعْقُوبُ مُبَشَّرًا بِهِ؛ لِأنَّ البِشارَةَ قَوْلٌ مَخْصُوصٌ، وهي أوَّلُ خَبَرٍ سارٍّ صادِقٍ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ [هود: ٧١] جُمْلَةٌ مُتَضَمِّنَةٌ بِهَذِهِ القُيُودِ، فَيَكُونُ بِشارَةً، بَلْ حَقِيقَةُ البِشارَةِ هي الجُمْلَةُ الخَبَرِيَّةُ. أوْ لَمّا كانَتِ البِشارَةُ قَوْلًا، كانَ مَوْضِعُ هَذِهِ الجُمْلَةِ نَصْبًا عَلى الحِكايَةِ بِالقَوْلِ، كَأنَّ المَعْنى: وقُلْنا لَها مِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ. والقائِلُ إذا قالَ: بَشَّرْتُ فُلانًا بِقُدُومِ أخِيهِ، وثِقْلِهِ في أثَرِهِ، لَمْ يُعْقَلْ مِنهُ إلّا بِشارَةٌ بِالأمْرَيْنِ جَمِيعًا. هَذا مِمّا لا يَسْتَرِيبُ ذُو فَهْمٍ فِيهِ البَتَّةَ. ثُمَّ يُضْعِفُ الجَرَّ أمْرٌ آخَرُ، وهو ضَعْفُ قَوْلِكَ: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ ومِن بَعْدِهِ عَمْرٍو؛ لِأنَّ العاطِفَ يَقُومُ حَرْفُ الجَرِّ، فَلا يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ المَجْرُورِ، كَما لا يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَ حَرْفِ الجارِّ والمَجْرُورِ. ويَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ أنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ لَمّا ذَكَرَ قِصَّةَ إبْراهِيمَ وابْنِهِ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ، قالَ: ﴿فَلَمّا أسْلَما وتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٣] ﴿ونادَيْناهُ أنْ يا إبْراهِيمُ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٤] ﴿قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيا إنّا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٥] ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَهو البَلاءُ المُبِينُ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٦] ﴿وفَدَيْناهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٧] ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١]. ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] (p-5055)، فَهَذا بِشارَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ لَهُ، شُكْرًا عَلى صَبْرِهِ عَلى ما أُمِرَ بِهِ. وهَذا ظاهِرٌ جِدًّا في أنَّ المُبَشَّرَ بِهِ غَيْرُ الأوَّلِ، بَلْ هو كالنَّصِّ فِيهِ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: فالبِشارَةُ الثّانِيَةُ وقَعَتْ عَلى نُبُوَّتِهِ، أيْ: لَمّا صَبَرَ الأبُ عَلى ما أُمِرَ بِهِ، وأسْلَمَ الوَلَدُ لِأمْرِ اللَّهِ، جازاهُ اللَّهُ عَلى ذَلِكَ بِأنْ أعْطاهُ النُّبُوَّةَ. قِيلَ: البِشارَةُ وقَعَتْ عَلى المَجْمُوعِ، عَلى ذاتِهِ ووُجُودِهِ وأنْ يَكُونَ نَبِيًّا؛ ولِهَذا يُنْصَبُ: {نَبِيًّا} عَلى الحالِ المُقَدَّرِ، أيْ: مُقَدَّرًا نُبُوَّتُهُ، فَلا يُمْكِنُ إخْراجُ البِشارَةِ أنْ يَقَعَ عَلى الأصْلِ، ثُمَّ يُخَصُّ بِالحالِ التّابِعَةِ الجارِيَةِ مَجْرى الفَضْلَةِ. هَذا مُحالٌ مِنَ الكَلامِ. بَلْ إذا وقَعَتِ البِشارَةُ عَلى نُبُوَّتِهِ، فَوُقُوعُها عَلى وُجُوهٍ أوْلى وأحْرى. وأيْضًا فَلا رَيْبَ أنَّ الذَّبِيحَ كانَ بِمَكَّةَ، ولِذَلِكَ جُعِلَتِ القَرابِينُ يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ، كَما جُعِلَ السَّعْيُ بَيْنَ الصَّفا والمَرْوَةِ ورَمْيُ الجِمارِ، تَذْكِيرًا لِشَأْنِ إسْماعِيلَ وأُمِّهِ، وإقامَةً لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ.

ومَعْلُومٌ أنَّ إسْماعِيلَ وأمَّهُ هُما اللَّذانِ كانا بِمَكَّةَ، دُونَ إسْحاقَ وأُمِّهِ، ولِهَذا اتَّصَلَ مَكانُ الذَّبْحِ وزَمانُهُ بِالبَيْتِ الحَرامِ الَّذِي اشْتَرَكَ في بِنائِهِ إبْراهِيمُ وإسْماعِيلُ، وكانَ النَّحْرُ بِمَكَّةَ مِن تَمامِ حَجِّ البَيْتِ الَّذِي كانَ عَلى يَدِ إبْراهِيمَ وابْنِهِ إسْماعِيلَ زَمانًا ومَكانًا. ولَوْ كانَ الذَّبْحُ بِالشّامِ، كَما يَزْعُمُ أهْلُ الكِتابِ ومَن تَلَقّى عَنْهُمْ، لَكانَتِ القَرابِينُ والنَّحْرُ بِالشّامِ لا بِمَكَّةَ. وأيْضًا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحانَهُ سَمّى الذَّبِيحَ حَلِيمًا؛ لِأنَّهُ لا أحْلَمَ مِمَّنْ أسْلَمَ نَفْسَهُ لِلذَّبْحِ طاعَةً لِرَبِّهِ. ولَمّا ذَكَرَ إسْحاقَ سَمّاهُ عَلِيمًا، فَقالَ: ﴿هَلْ أتاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إبْراهِيمَ المُكْرَمِينَ﴾ [الذاريات: ٢٤] ﴿إذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقالُوا سَلامًا قالَ سَلامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ﴾ [الذاريات: ٢٥] إلى أنْ قالَ: ﴿قالُوا لا تَخَفْ وبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾ [الذاريات: ٢٨]. وهَذا إسْحاقُ بِلا رَيْبٍ، لِأنَّهُ مِن امْرَأتِهِ وهي المُبَشَّرَةُ بِهِ، وأمّا إسْماعِيلُ فَمِنَ السُّرِّيَّةِ.

وأيْضًا فَإنَّهُما بُشِّرا بِهِ عَلى الكِبَرِ واليَأْسِ (p-5056) مِنَ الوَلَدِ. وهَذا بِخِلافِ إسْماعِيلَ فَإنَّهُ وُلِدَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ. وأيْضًا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحانَهُ أجْرى العادَةَ البَشَرِيَّةَ أنَّ بِكْرَ الأوْلادِ أحَبُّ إلى الوالِدَيْنِ مِمَّنْ بَعْدَهُ. وإبْراهِيمُ لَمّا سَألَ رَبَّهُ الوَلَدَ ووَهَبَهُ لَهُ، تَعَلَّقَتْ شُعْبَةٌ مِن قَلْبِهِ بِمَحَبَّتِهِ، واللَّهُ تَعالى قَدِ اتَّخَذَهُ خَلِيلًا (khullah: intimate friendship with God). والخِلَّةُ مَنصِبٌ يَقْتَضِي تَوْحِيدَ المَحْبُوبِ بِالمَحَبَّةِ، وأنْ لا يُشارَكَ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ غَيْرِهِ فِيها. فَلَمّا أخَذَ الوَلَدُ شُعْبَةً مِن قَلْبِ الوالِدِ، جاءَتْ غَيْرَةُ الخِلَّةِ تَنْتَزِعُها مِن قَلْبِ الخَلِيلِ، فَأمَرَهُ الجَلِيلُ بِذَبْحِ المَحْبُوبِ. فَلَمّا أقْدَمَ عَلى ذَبْحِهِ، وكانَتْ مَحَبَّةُ اللَّهِ أعْظَمَ عِنْدَهُ مِن مَحَبَّةِ الوَلَدِ، خَلُصَتِ الخِلَّةُ حِينَئِذٍ مِن شَوائِبِ المُشارَكَةِ، فَلَمْ يَبْقَ في الذَّبْحِ مَصْلَحَةٌ؛ إذْ كانَتِ المَصْلَحَةُ إنَّما هي في العَزْمِ وتَوْطِينِ النَّفْسِ فِيهِ، فَقَدْ حَصَلَ المَقْصُودُ، فَنُسِخَ الأمْرُ، وفُدِيَ الذَّبِيحُ، وصَدَقَ الخَلِيلُ الرُّؤْيا، وحَصَلَ مُرادُ الرَّبِّ.

ومَعْلُومٌ أنَّ هَذا الِامْتِحانَ والِاخْتِبارَ إنَّما حَصَلَ عِنْدَ أوَّلِ مَوْلُودٍ، ولَمْ يَكُنْ لِيَحْصُلَ في المَوْلُودِ الآخَرِ دُونَ الأوَّلِ، بَلْ لَمْ يَحْصُلْ عِنْدَ المَوْلُودِ الآخَرِ مِن مُزاحَمَةِ الخِلَّةِ ما يَقْتَضِي الأمْرَ بِذَبْحِهِ. وهَذا في غايَةِ الظُّهُورِ. وأيْضًا فَإنَّ سارَّةَ امْرَأةَ الخَلِيلِ غارَتْ مِن هاجَرَ وابْنِها أشَدَّ الغَيْرَةِ، فَإنَّها كانَتْ جارِيَةً، فَلَمّا ولَدَتْ إسْماعِيلَ وأحَبَّهُ أبُوهُ اشْتَدَّتْ غَيْرَةُ سارَّةَ. فَأمَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ أنْ يُبْعِدَ عَنْها هاجَرَ وابْنَها ويُسْكِنَها في أرْضِ مَكَّةَ، لِيُبْرِدَ عَنْ سارَّةَ حَرارَةَ الغَيْرَةِ. وهَذا مِن رَحْمَتِهِ ورَأْفَتِهِ. فَكَيْفَ يَأْمُرُهُ سُبْحانَهُ بَعْدَ هَذا أنْ يَذْبَحَ ابْنَها، ويَدَعَ ابْنَ الجارِيَةِ بِحالِهِ هَذا، مَعَ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ لَها، وإبْعادِ الضَّرَرِ عَنْها وخَيْرَتِهِ لَها؟ فَكَيْفَ يَأْمُرُ بَعْدَ هَذا بِذَبْحِ ابْنِها دُونَ ابْنِ الجارِيَةِ؟

Rather, His perfect wisdom required that He command the slaughter of the slave-girl's son. Then the heart of the mistress would soften toward her child, the harshness of jealousy would turn into mercy, and she would see the blessing of this slave-girl and her son, and that God does not waste a household: this one and her son are of them. His servants would see His mending after breaking, His kindness after hardship, and that the outcome of the patience of Hajar and her son, through distance, loneliness, estrangement, and submission, leading up to the slaughter of the boy, ended in what it ended in: making their traces and the place where their feet trod into rites for the worship of the believers, and places of worship for them until the Day of Resurrection. This is the way of God, exalted is He, with whoever He wills to elevate among His creation: that He bestows favor upon him after his weakness, humiliation, and brokenness. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors﴾ [al-Qasas: 5]. ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 4]. End of quotation.

[p-5057]

Al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): Those who hold that the one who was sacrificed was Isma'il have relied on His saying, exalted is He, afterward: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq﴾ [al-Saffat: 112]. This view, which a group of scholars preferred, is supported by several proofs: among them the description of him (Isma'il) as forbearing, and the mention of the good news of Ishaq after it, and the good news of Ya'qub being from behind Ishaq, and other things. These are speculative matters, not definitive ones. Then he said: I reflected on the Qur'an and found in it what requires certainty or comes close to it, and I have not seen anyone before me derive it: that the good news occurred twice. The first time in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I will go to my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [al-Saffat: 99]; ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous﴾ [al-Saffat: 100]; ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy﴾ [al-Saffat: 101]; ﴿And when he reached with him the age of exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I sacrifice you"﴾ [al-Saffat: 102]. This verse is decisive that this one given the good news was the one to be sacrificed. The second time in His saying: ﴿And his wife was standing, and she laughed. So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71], and the verse continues. In it he clearly states that the one given the good news was Ishaq, and this was not in answer to a request from Ibrahim. Rather, his wife said that she was an old woman and he was an old man. That was in al-Sham, when the angels came to him concerning the people of Lut, and it was at the end of his life. As for the first good news, it was when he moved from Iraq to al-Sham, when his age was one in which a child was not considered unusual, and for that reason he asked for it. Thus we know from this that there were two good tidings at two times, for two boys: one of them without a request, and that is explicitly Ishaq; and the second, before that, in answer to a request, and that is someone other than him. Therefore we are certain that he is Isma'il, and he is the one sacrificed. End of quotation.

القَوْلُ في تَأْوِيلِ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى:
[ ١٠٨ - ١١٣ ] ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١] ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] ﴿وبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ وعَلى إسْحاقَ ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِما مُحْسِنٌ وظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ مُبِينٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] .
(p-5052) ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] أي: مِثْلَ ما تَرَكْنا عَلى نُوحٍ، كَما تَقَدَّمَ بَيانُهُ وإعْرابُهُ (i'rab: the grammatical analysis of the Arabic words). ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١] ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] ﴿وبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: عَلى إبْراهِيمَ. ﴿وعَلى إسْحاقَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: بِتَكْثِيرِ الذُّرِّيَّةِ وتَسَلْسُلِ النُّبُوَّةِ فِيهِمْ، وجَعْلِهِمْ مُلُوكًا، وإيتائِهِمْ ما لَمْ يُؤْتَ أحَدٌ. ﴿ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِما مُحْسِنٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: في عَمَلِهِ. ﴿وظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: بِالكُفْرِ والمَعاصِي. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: ظاهِرُ الظُّلْمِ.

تَنْبِيهاتٌ:

الأوَّلُ: يَرْوِي المُفَسِّرُونَ هَهُنا في قِصَّةِ الذَّبْحِ رِواياتٍ مُنْكَرَةً لَمْ يَصِحَّ سَنَدُها ولا مَتْنُها، بَلْ ولَمْ تَحْسُنْ، فَهي مُعْضِلَةٌ تَنْتَهِي إلى السُّدِّيِّ وكَعْبٍ. والسُّدِّيُّ حالُهُ مَعْلُومٌ في ضَعْفِ مَرْوِيّاتِهِ، وكَذَلِكَ كَعْبٌ.

قالَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: لَمّا أسْلَمَ كَعْبُ الأحْبارِ في الدَّوْلَةِ العُمَرِيَّةِ، جَعَلَ يُحَدِّثُ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ كُتُبِهِ قَدِيمًا، فَرُبَّما اسْتَمَعَ لَهُ عُمَرُ، فَتَرَخَّصَ النّاسُ في اسْتِماعِ ما عِنْدَهُ عَنْهُ، غَثِّها وسَمِينِها، ولَيْسَ لِهَذِهِ الأُمَّةِ حاجَةٌ إلى حَرْفٍ واحِدٍ مِمّا عِنْدَهُ. انْتَهى.

ولَقَدْ صَدَقَ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ، ولِذا نَرى التَّزَيُّدَ عَلى أصْلِ ما قَصَّ في التَّنْزِيلِ مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ لَهُ، إلّا إذا صَحَّ سَنَدُهُ، أوِ اطْمَأنَّ القَلْبُ بِهِ. وقَدْ ولِعَ الخُطَباءُ في دَواوِينِهِمْ بِرِوايَةِ هَذِهِ القِصَّةِ في خُطْبَةِ الأضْحى مِن طُرُقِها الواهِيَةِ عِنْدَ المُحَدِّثِينَ، ويَرَوْنَها ضَرْبَةَ لازِبٍ عَلى ضَعْفِ سَنَدِها، وكَوْنِ مَتْنِها مُنْكَرًا أيْضًا أوْ مَوْضُوعًا. ولَمّا صَنَّفْتُ مَجْمُوعَةَ الخُطَبِ حَذَفْتُ هَذِهِ الرِّوايَةَ مِن خُطْبَةِ الأضْحى كَكُلِّ مَرْوِيٍّ ضَعِيفٍ في فَضائِلِ الشُّهُورِ والأوْقاتِ، واقْتَصَرْتُ عَلى جِيادِ الأخْبارِ والآثارِ، وذَلِكَ مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْنا فَلا نُحْصِي ثَناءً عَلَيْهِ.

وأمْثَلُ ما رُوِيَ في هَذا النَّبَأِ مِنَ (p-5053) الآثارِ ما أخْرَجَهُ الإمامُ أحْمَدُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُما مَوْقُوفًا، قالَ: لَمّا أُمِرَ إبْراهِيمُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ بِالمَناسِكِ، عَرَضَ لَهُ الشَّيْطانُ عِنْدَ السَّعْيِ، فَسابَقَهُ فَسَبَقَهُ إبْراهِيمُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلاةُ والسَّلامُ إلى جَمْرَةِ العَقَبَةِ، فَعَرَضَ لَهُ الشَّيْطانُ فَرَماهُ بِسَبْعِ حَصَياتٍ حَتّى ذَهَبَ، ثُمَّ عَرَضَ لَهُ عِنْدَ الجَمْرَةِ الوُسْطى فَرَماهُ بِسَبْعِ حَصَياتٍ، ثُمَّ تَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ، وعَلى إسْماعِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَمِيصٌ أبْيَضُ، فَقالَ لَهُ: يا أبَتِ! إنَّهُ لَيْسَ لِي ثَوْبٌ تُكَفِّنُنِي فِيهِ غَيْرُهُ، فاخْلَعْهُ حَتّى تُكَفِّنَنِي فِيهِ، فَعالَجَهُ لِيُخْلِصَهُ، فَنُودِيَ مِن خَلْفِهِ: أنْ يا إبْراهِيمُ قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيا. فالتَفَتَ إبْراهِيمُ فَإذا بِكَبْشٍ أبْيَضَ أقْرَنَ أعْيَنَ. قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: لَقَدْ رَأيْتُنا نَتَتَبَّعُ ذَلِكَ الضَّرْبَ مِنَ الكِباشِ.

الثّانِي: قالَ السُّيُوطِيُّ في (الإكْلِيلِ): في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ أنَّ رُؤْيا الأنْبِياءِ وحْيٌ، وجَوازُ نَسْخِ الفِعْلِ قَبْلَ التَّمَكُّنِ (naskh: abrogation of a ruling before it is carried out)، وتَقْدِيمُ المَشِيئَةِ في كُلِّ قَوْلٍ، واسْتَدَلَّ بَعْضُهم بِهَذِهِ القِصَّةِ عَلى أنَّ مَن نَذَرَ ذَبْحَ ولَدِهِ، لَزِمَهُ ذَبْحُ شاةٍ.

ثُمَّ قالَ السُّيُوطِيُّ: فُسِّرَ الذِّبْحُ العَظِيمُ في الأحادِيثِ والآثارِ بِكَبْشٍ، فاسْتَدَلَّ بِهِ المالِكِيَّةُ عَلى أنَّ الغَنَمَ في التَّضْحِيَةِ أفْضَلُ مِنَ الإبِلِ. انْتَهى.

الثّالِثُ: اُسْتُدِلَّ بِالآيَةِ عَلى أنَّهُ تَعالى قَدْ يَأْمُرُ بِما لا يُرِيدُ وُقُوعَهُ، كَما ذَكَرَهُ الرّازِيُّ، وذَلِكَ في بابِ الِابْتِلاءِ، أيِ: ابْتِلاءِ المَأْمُورِ في إخْلاصِهِ وصِدْقِهِ، فِيما يَشُقُّ عَلى النَّفْسِ تَحَمُّلُهُ.

الرّابِعُ: يَذْكُرُ كَثِيرٌ الخِلافَ في الذَّبِيحِ. قالَ الإمامُ ابْنُ القَيِّمِ في (زادِ المَعادِ): وإسْماعِيلُ هو الذَّبِيحُ عَلى القَوْلِ الصَّوابِ عِنْدَ عُلَماءِ الصَّحابَةِ والتّابِعِينَ ومَن بَعْدَهُمْ، وأمّا القَوْلُ بِأنَّهُ إسْحاقُ فَباطِلٌ بِأكْثَرَ مِن عِشْرِينَ وجْهًا. وسَمِعْتُ شَيْخَ الإسْلامِ ابْنَ تَيْمِيَةَ قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ رُوحَهُ يَقُولُ: هَذا القَوْلُ إنَّما هو مُتَلَقًّى مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ، مَعَ أنَّهُ باطِلٌ بِنَصِّ كِتابِهِمْ؛ فَإنَّ فِيهِ إنَّ اللَّهَ أمَرَ (p-5054) إبْراهِيمَ أنْ يَذْبَحَ ابْنَهُ (بِكْرَهُ)، وفي لَفْظٍ: (وحِيدَهُ)، ولا يَشُكُّ أهْلُ الكِتابِ مَعَ المُسْلِمِينَ أنَّ إسْماعِيلَ هو بِكْرُ أوْلادِهِ.

والَّذِي غَرَّ أصْحابَ هَذا القَوْلِ أنَّ في التَّوْراةِ الَّتِي بِأيْدِيهِمْ: (اذْبَحِ ابْنَكَ إسْحاقَ).

قالَ: وهَذِهِ الزِّيادَةُ مِن تَحْرِيفِهِمْ وكَذِبِهِمْ؛ لِأنَّها تُناقِضُ قَوْلَهُ: بِكْرَكَ، وحِيدَكَ. ولَكِنَّ يَهُودَ حَسَدَتْ بَنِي إسْماعِيلَ عَلى هَذا الشَّرَفِ، وأحَبُّوا أنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمْ، وأنْ يَسُوقُوهُ إلَيْهِمْ، ويَخْتارُوهُ دُونَ العَرَبِ. ويَأْبى اللَّهُ إلّا أنْ يَجْعَلَ فَضْلَهُ لِأهْلِهِ. وكَيْفَ يُسَوَّغُ أنْ يُقالَ إنَّ الذَّبِيحَ إسْحاقُ، واللَّهُ تَعالى قَدْ بَشَّرَ أُمَّ إسْحاقَ بِهِ وبِابْنِهِ يَعْقُوبَ، فَقالَ تَعالى عَنِ المَلائِكَةِ أنَّهم قالُوا لِإبْراهِيمَ لَمّا أتَوْهُ بِالبُشْرى: ﴿لا تَخَفْ إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾ [هود: ٧٠] ﴿وامْرَأتُهُ قائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْناها بِإسْحاقَ ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ [هود: ٧١]. فَمُحالٌ أنْ يُبَشِّرَها بِأنَّهُ يَكُونُ لَها ولَدٌ ثُمَّ يَأْمُرُ بِذَبْحِهِ. ولا رَيْبَ أنَّ يَعْقُوبَ داخِلٌ في البِشارَةِ، فَتَناوُلُ البِشارَةِ لِإسْحاقَ ويَعْقُوبَ في اللَّفْظِ واحِدٌ. وهَذا ظاهِرُ الكَلامِ وسِياقُهُ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: لَوْ كانَ الأمْرُ كَما ذَكَرْتُمُوهُ لَكانَ يَعْقُوبُ مَجْرُورًا عَطْفًا عَلى إسْحاقَ، فَكانَتِ القِراءَةُ: ﴿ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ [هود: ٧١] أيْ: ويَعْقُوبُ مِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ. قِيلَ: لا يَمْنَعُ الرَّفْعُ أنْ يَكُونَ يَعْقُوبُ مُبَشَّرًا بِهِ؛ لِأنَّ البِشارَةَ قَوْلٌ مَخْصُوصٌ، وهي أوَّلُ خَبَرٍ سارٍّ صادِقٍ.

وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ [هود: ٧١] جُمْلَةٌ مُتَضَمِّنَةٌ بِهَذِهِ القُيُودِ، فَيَكُونُ بِشارَةً، بَلْ حَقِيقَةُ البِشارَةِ هي الجُمْلَةُ الخَبَرِيَّةُ. أوْ لَمّا كانَتِ البِشارَةُ قَوْلًا، كانَ مَوْضِعُ هَذِهِ الجُمْلَةِ نَصْبًا عَلى الحِكايَةِ بِالقَوْلِ، كَأنَّ المَعْنى: وقُلْنا لَها مِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ. والقائِلُ إذا قالَ: بَشَّرْتُ فُلانًا بِقُدُومِ أخِيهِ، وثِقْلِهِ في أثَرِهِ، لَمْ يُعْقَلْ مِنهُ إلّا بِشارَةٌ بِالأمْرَيْنِ جَمِيعًا. هَذا مِمّا لا يَسْتَرِيبُ ذُو فَهْمٍ فِيهِ البَتَّةَ. ثُمَّ يُضْعِفُ الجَرَّ أمْرٌ آخَرُ، وهو ضَعْفُ قَوْلِكَ: مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ ومِن بَعْدِهِ عَمْرٍو؛ لِأنَّ العاطِفَ يَقُومُ حَرْفُ الجَرِّ، فَلا يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ المَجْرُورِ، كَما لا يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَ حَرْفِ الجارِّ والمَجْرُورِ. ويَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ أنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ لَمّا ذَكَرَ قِصَّةَ إبْراهِيمَ وابْنِهِ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ، قالَ: ﴿فَلَمّا أسْلَما وتَلَّهُ لِلْجَبِينِ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٣] ﴿ونادَيْناهُ أنْ يا إبْراهِيمُ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٤] ﴿قَدْ صَدَّقْتَ الرُّؤْيا إنّا كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٥] ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَهو البَلاءُ المُبِينُ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٦] ﴿وفَدَيْناهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٧] ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١]. ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] (p-5055)، فَهَذا بِشارَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ لَهُ، شُكْرًا عَلى صَبْرِهِ عَلى ما أُمِرَ بِهِ. وهَذا ظاهِرٌ جِدًّا في أنَّ المُبَشَّرَ بِهِ غَيْرُ الأوَّلِ، بَلْ هو كالنَّصِّ فِيهِ.

فَإنْ قِيلَ: فالبِشارَةُ الثّانِيَةُ وقَعَتْ عَلى نُبُوَّتِهِ، أيْ: لَمّا صَبَرَ الأبُ عَلى ما أُمِرَ بِهِ، وأسْلَمَ الوَلَدُ لِأمْرِ اللَّهِ، جازاهُ اللَّهُ عَلى ذَلِكَ بِأنْ أعْطاهُ النُّبُوَّةَ. قِيلَ: البِشارَةُ وقَعَتْ عَلى المَجْمُوعِ، عَلى ذاتِهِ ووُجُودِهِ وأنْ يَكُونَ نَبِيًّا؛ ولِهَذا يُنْصَبُ: {نَبِيًّا} عَلى الحالِ المُقَدَّرِ، أيْ: مُقَدَّرًا نُبُوَّتُهُ، فَلا يُمْكِنُ إخْراجُ البِشارَةِ أنْ يَقَعَ عَلى الأصْلِ، ثُمَّ يُخَصُّ بِالحالِ التّابِعَةِ الجارِيَةِ مَجْرى الفَضْلَةِ. هَذا مُحالٌ مِنَ الكَلامِ. بَلْ إذا وقَعَتِ البِشارَةُ عَلى نُبُوَّتِهِ، فَوُقُوعُها عَلى وُجُوهٍ أوْلى وأحْرى. وأيْضًا فَلا رَيْبَ أنَّ الذَّبِيحَ كانَ بِمَكَّةَ، ولِذَلِكَ جُعِلَتِ القَرابِينُ يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ، كَما جُعِلَ السَّعْيُ بَيْنَ الصَّفا والمَرْوَةِ ورَمْيُ الجِمارِ، تَذْكِيرًا لِشَأْنِ إسْماعِيلَ وأُمِّهِ، وإقامَةً لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ.

ومَعْلُومٌ أنَّ إسْماعِيلَ وأمَّهُ هُما اللَّذانِ كانا بِمَكَّةَ، دُونَ إسْحاقَ وأُمِّهِ، ولِهَذا اتَّصَلَ مَكانُ الذَّبْحِ وزَمانُهُ بِالبَيْتِ الحَرامِ الَّذِي اشْتَرَكَ في بِنائِهِ إبْراهِيمُ وإسْماعِيلُ، وكانَ النَّحْرُ بِمَكَّةَ مِن تَمامِ حَجِّ البَيْتِ الَّذِي كانَ عَلى يَدِ إبْراهِيمَ وابْنِهِ إسْماعِيلَ زَمانًا ومَكانًا. ولَوْ كانَ الذَّبْحُ بِالشّامِ، كَما يَزْعُمُ أهْلُ الكِتابِ ومَن تَلَقّى عَنْهُمْ، لَكانَتِ القَرابِينُ والنَّحْرُ بِالشّامِ لا بِمَكَّةَ. وأيْضًا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحانَهُ سَمّى الذَّبِيحَ حَلِيمًا؛ لِأنَّهُ لا أحْلَمَ مِمَّنْ أسْلَمَ نَفْسَهُ لِلذَّبْحِ طاعَةً لِرَبِّهِ. ولَمّا ذَكَرَ إسْحاقَ سَمّاهُ عَلِيمًا، فَقالَ: ﴿هَلْ أتاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إبْراهِيمَ المُكْرَمِينَ﴾ [الذاريات: ٢٤] ﴿إذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقالُوا سَلامًا قالَ سَلامٌ قَوْمٌ مُنْكَرُونَ﴾ [الذاريات: ٢٥] إلى أنْ قالَ: ﴿قالُوا لا تَخَفْ وبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلامٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾ [الذاريات: ٢٨]. وهَذا إسْحاقُ بِلا رَيْبٍ، لِأنَّهُ مِن امْرَأتِهِ وهي المُبَشَّرَةُ بِهِ، وأمّا إسْماعِيلُ فَمِنَ السُّرِّيَّةِ.

وأيْضًا فَإنَّهُما بُشِّرا بِهِ عَلى الكِبَرِ واليَأْسِ (p-5056) مِنَ الوَلَدِ. وهَذا بِخِلافِ إسْماعِيلَ فَإنَّهُ وُلِدَ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ. وأيْضًا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحانَهُ أجْرى العادَةَ البَشَرِيَّةَ أنَّ بِكْرَ الأوْلادِ أحَبُّ إلى الوالِدَيْنِ مِمَّنْ بَعْدَهُ. وإبْراهِيمُ لَمّا سَألَ رَبَّهُ الوَلَدَ ووَهَبَهُ لَهُ، تَعَلَّقَتْ شُعْبَةٌ مِن قَلْبِهِ بِمَحَبَّتِهِ، واللَّهُ تَعالى قَدِ اتَّخَذَهُ خَلِيلًا (khullah: intimate friendship with God). والخِلَّةُ مَنصِبٌ يَقْتَضِي تَوْحِيدَ المَحْبُوبِ بِالمَحَبَّةِ، وأنْ لا يُشارَكَ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ غَيْرِهِ فِيها. فَلَمّا أخَذَ الوَلَدُ شُعْبَةً مِن قَلْبِ الوالِدِ، جاءَتْ غَيْرَةُ الخِلَّةِ تَنْتَزِعُها مِن قَلْبِ الخَلِيلِ، فَأمَرَهُ الجَلِيلُ بِذَبْحِ المَحْبُوبِ. فَلَمّا أقْدَمَ عَلى ذَبْحِهِ، وكانَتْ مَحَبَّةُ اللَّهِ أعْظَمَ عِنْدَهُ مِن مَحَبَّةِ الوَلَدِ، خَلُصَتِ الخِلَّةُ حِينَئِذٍ مِن شَوائِبِ المُشارَكَةِ، فَلَمْ يَبْقَ في الذَّبْحِ مَصْلَحَةٌ؛ إذْ كانَتِ المَصْلَحَةُ إنَّما هي في العَزْمِ وتَوْطِينِ النَّفْسِ فِيهِ، فَقَدْ حَصَلَ المَقْصُودُ، فَنُسِخَ الأمْرُ، وفُدِيَ الذَّبِيحُ، وصَدَقَ الخَلِيلُ الرُّؤْيا، وحَصَلَ مُرادُ الرَّبِّ.

ومَعْلُومٌ أنَّ هَذا الِامْتِحانَ والِاخْتِبارَ إنَّما حَصَلَ عِنْدَ أوَّلِ مَوْلُودٍ، ولَمْ يَكُنْ لِيَحْصُلَ في المَوْلُودِ الآخَرِ دُونَ الأوَّلِ، بَلْ لَمْ يَحْصُلْ عِنْدَ المَوْلُودِ الآخَرِ مِن مُزاحَمَةِ الخِلَّةِ ما يَقْتَضِي الأمْرَ بِذَبْحِهِ. وهَذا في غايَةِ الظُّهُورِ. وأيْضًا فَإنَّ سارَّةَ امْرَأةَ الخَلِيلِ غارَتْ مِن هاجَرَ وابْنِها أشَدَّ الغَيْرَةِ، فَإنَّها كانَتْ جارِيَةً، فَلَمّا ولَدَتْ إسْماعِيلَ وأحَبَّهُ أبُوهُ اشْتَدَّتْ غَيْرَةُ سارَّةَ. فَأمَرَ اللَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ أنْ يُبْعِدَ عَنْها هاجَرَ وابْنَها ويُسْكِنَها في أرْضِ مَكَّةَ، لِيُبْرِدَ عَنْ سارَّةَ حَرارَةَ الغَيْرَةِ. وهَذا مِن رَحْمَتِهِ ورَأْفَتِهِ. فَكَيْفَ يَأْمُرُهُ سُبْحانَهُ بَعْدَ هَذا أنْ يَذْبَحَ ابْنَها، ويَدَعَ ابْنَ الجارِيَةِ بِحالِهِ هَذا، مَعَ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ لَها، وإبْعادِ الضَّرَرِ عَنْها وخَيْرَتِهِ لَها؟ فَكَيْفَ يَأْمُرُ بَعْدَ هَذا بِذَبْحِ ابْنِها دُونَ ابْنِ الجارِيَةِ؟

Rather, His perfect wisdom required that He command the slaughter of the slave-girl's son. Then the heart of the mistress would soften toward her child, the harshness of jealousy would turn into mercy, and she would see the blessing of this slave-girl and her son, and that God does not waste a household: this one and her son are of them. His servants would see His mending after breaking, His kindness after hardship, and that the outcome of the patience of Hajar and her son, through distance, loneliness, estrangement, and submission, leading up to the slaughter of the boy, ended in what it ended in: making their traces and the place where their feet trod into rites for the worship of the believers, and places of worship for them until the Day of Resurrection. This is the way of God, exalted is He, with whoever He wills to elevate among His creation: that He bestows favor upon him after his weakness, humiliation, and brokenness. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We wished to confer favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors﴾ [al-Qasas: 5]. ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 4]. End of quotation.

[p-5057]

Al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): Those who hold that the one who was sacrificed was Isma'il have relied on His saying, exalted is He, afterward: ﴿And We gave him the good news of Ishaq﴾ [al-Saffat: 112]. This view, which a group of scholars preferred, is supported by several proofs: among them the description of him (Isma'il) as forbearing, and the mention of the good news of Ishaq after it, and the good news of Ya'qub being from behind Ishaq, and other things. These are speculative matters, not definitive ones. Then he said: I reflected on the Qur'an and found in it what requires certainty or comes close to it, and I have not seen anyone before me derive it: that the good news occurred twice. The first time in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I will go to my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [al-Saffat: 99]; ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous﴾ [al-Saffat: 100]; ﴿So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy﴾ [al-Saffat: 101]; ﴿And when he reached with him the age of exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I sacrifice you"﴾ [al-Saffat: 102]. This verse is decisive that this one given the good news was the one to be sacrificed. The second time in His saying: ﴿And his wife was standing, and she laughed. So We gave her good tidings of Ishaq and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ [Hud: 71], and the verse continues. In it he clearly states that the one given the good news was Ishaq, and this was not in answer to a request from Ibrahim. Rather, his wife said that she was an old woman and he was an old man. That was in al-Sham, when the angels came to him concerning the people of Lut, and it was at the end of his life. As for the first good news, it was when he moved from Iraq to al-Sham, when his age was one in which a child was not considered unusual, and for that reason he asked for it. Thus we know from this that there were two good tidings at two times, for two boys: one of them without a request, and that is explicitly Ishaq; and the second, before that, in answer to a request, and that is someone other than him. Therefore we are certain that he is Isma'il, and he is the one sacrificed. End of quotation.

القَوْلُ في تَأْوِيلِ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى:
[ ١٠٨ - ١١٣ ] ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١] ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] ﴿وبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ وعَلى إسْحاقَ ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِما مُحْسِنٌ وظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ مُبِينٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] .
(p-5052) ﴿وتَرَكْنا عَلَيْهِ في الآخِرِينَ﴾ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلى إبْراهِيمَ﴾ [الصافات: ١٠٩] أي: مِثْلَ ما تَرَكْنا عَلى نُوحٍ، كَما تَقَدَّمَ بَيانُهُ وإعْرابُهُ (i'rab: the grammatical analysis of the Arabic words). ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٠] ﴿إنَّهُ مِن عِبادِنا المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١١] ﴿وبَشَّرْناهُ بِإسْحاقَ نَبِيًّا مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٢] ﴿وبارَكْنا عَلَيْهِ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: عَلى إبْراهِيمَ. ﴿وعَلى إسْحاقَ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: بِتَكْثِيرِ الذُّرِّيَّةِ وتَسَلْسُلِ النُّبُوَّةِ فِيهِمْ، وجَعْلِهِمْ مُلُوكًا، وإيتائِهِمْ ما لَمْ يُؤْتَ أحَدٌ. ﴿ومِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِما مُحْسِنٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: في عَمَلِهِ. ﴿وظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: بِالكُفْرِ والمَعاصِي. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ [الصافات: ١١٣] أي: ظاهِرُ الظُّلْمِ.

تَنْبِيهاتٌ:

الأوَّلُ: يَرْوِي المُفَسِّرُونَ هَهُنا في قِصَّةِ الذَّبْحِ رِواياتٍ مُنْكَرَةً لَمْ يَصِحَّ سَنَدُها ولا مَتْنُها، بَلْ ولَمْ تَحْسُنْ، فَهي مُعْضِلَةٌ تَنْتَهِي إلى السُّدِّيِّ وكَعْبٍ. والسُّدِّيُّ حالُهُ مَعْلُومٌ في ضَعْفِ مَرْوِيّاتِهِ، وكَذَلِكَ كَعْبٌ.

قالَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ: لَمّا أسْلَمَ كَعْبُ الأحْبارِ في الدَّوْلَةِ العُمَرِيَّةِ، جَعَلَ يُحَدِّثُ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ عَنْ كُتُبِهِ قَدِيمًا، فَرُبَّما اسْتَمَعَ لَهُ عُمَرُ، فَتَرَخَّصَ النّاسُ في اسْتِماعِ ما عِنْدَهُ عَنْهُ، غَثِّها وسَمِينِها، ولَيْسَ لِهَذِهِ الأُمَّةِ حاجَةٌ إلى حَرْفٍ واحِدٍ مِمّا عِنْدَهُ. انْتَهى.
