Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[153] ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾

﴿Has He chosen daughters﴾, that is, He chose the females, ﴿over sons﴾, that is, the males.

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 154:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[154] ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾

﴿What is the matter with you?﴾ That is: what has befallen your intellects? ﴿How do you judge?﴾ By attributing the deficient to the Most High station, and by choosing the perfect for yourselves.

(p-5065) A subtle point (latifa):

Al-Zamakhshari said: He said: I say: ﴿Has He chosen daughters...﴾ [al-Saffat: 153], with a fatha on the hamza, is an interrogative in the manner of denial and disapproval. How then is the qira'a (canonical mode of recitation) of Abu Ja'far, with a kasra on the hamza, sound as an affirmation? I say: he takes it as part of the speech of the disbelievers, replacing their saying: ﴿God has begotten children﴾ [al-Saffat: 152]. Hamza and al-A'mash, may Allah be pleased with them both, also recited it this way. This recitation, although this is its intended meaning, is weak. What weakens it is that denial surrounds this sentence on both of its sides. That is His saying: ﴿And indeed they are liars﴾ [al-Saffat: 152], and: ﴿What is the matter with you? How do you judge?﴾. So whoever makes it an affirmation has placed it as an intruder between two connected parts. End.

The Interpretation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[155] ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾

﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ That is: He is exalted above that.

The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[156] ﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾

﴿Or do you have a clear authority?﴾ That is: a manifest proof and a decisive argument. Then it is not permissible that this be rational, since it is impossible by reason when one examines it; its utmost (possibility) is that it be transmitted from sacred books.

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[157] ﴿So bring your Book, if you are truthful.﴾

﴿So bring your Book﴾, i.e., the one in which that is written, derived from a heavenly revelation. ﴿If you are truthful﴾, i.e., in your claim. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they have been associating [with Allah]?﴾ [ar-Rum: 35]. And in it is an indication that the basis of a claim rests upon clear proof, and that without it, it carries no weight.

(p-5066) The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[158] ﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship. But the jinn know well that they will be brought forth (to punishment).﴾

﴿And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship﴾ means: a closeness to Him. Mujahid said: The polytheists said, "The angels are the daughters of Allah, exalted is He." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Then who are their mothers?" They said: "The daughters of the chiefs of the jinn." Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the same. Then (the Qur'an) indicates that no relationship that could imply lineage exists in any way, by way of the impossibility of that according to reason, with His saying: ﴿But the jinn know well﴾, that is, those to whom this lineage is attributed, ﴿that they will be brought forth﴾, that is, into the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. This is because the jinn, like the jinn (in the sense of a name), are in most usage a designation for the wicked group who disobeyed the command of their Lord from the world of the devils. That is: those to whom it is attributed disown this relationship, because they know from themselves that they are among the people of the Blaze, not from the world of the pure spirits. So what is the matter with these polytheists, who speak about what they do not know? Some have interpreted "the jinn" as the angels mentioned earlier. The pronoun in ﴿they﴾ refers to the disbelievers. Perhaps what we have mentioned is better, because it is free of scattering the pronouns and because it agrees with the most common usage of "jinn" and "jinna". This applies to other than the angels. We said "most common" because of what has been heard of applying "jinn" to the angels.

Al-A'sha said, mentioning Sulayman, peace be upon him:

*And he subjugated from the jinn of the angels nine, standing before him, working as servants (mihrab-like?) ...*

(The verse, as it stands in the text, reads:)
*And he subjugated from the jinn of the angels nine, standing before him, working, carrying out his commands.*

Al-Raghib (al-Raghib al-Isfahani) said: "Jinn" is used in two senses. One: for the spiritual beings hidden from all the senses, in contrast to humankind. In this sense the angels are included. It has been said: rather, the jinn are a part of the spiritual beings, because the spiritual beings are of three kinds: the good, who are the angels; the evil, who are the devils; and the intermediate, among whom are good and evil, who are the jinn. This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me that a company of the jinn listened"﴾ [al-Jinn: 1] up to His saying: ﴿And among us are the unjust﴾ [al-Jinn: 14]. End of quotation.

Al-Fasi (al-'Allama al-Fasi), in his commentary on al-Qamus (the Dictionary), rejected the application of "jinn" to the angels. He said: Explaining the jinn as the angels is rejected, since the angels were created from light, not from fire as the jinn were. The angels are infallible, do not reproduce, and are not characterized by maleness or femaleness, unlike (p-5067) the jinn. For this reason, the majority of scholars said that the exception in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿except Iblis﴾, is either disjunctive (munqati', an exception not belonging to the same category) or connected (muttasil, an exception belonging to the same category), because he was immersed among them and took on their characteristics. End of quotation.

This supports what we have held, and the verse of al-A'sha is not valid as evidence, because its referent is incorrect: Sulayman's subjugation of the angels did not involve them building structures for him, and that is not their work, peace be upon them. The discussion of this has already passed in the commentary on Surat Saba'.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[159] ﴿Glory be to God above what they describe﴾.

﴿Glory be to God above what they describe﴾: that is, above what they attribute to Him of offspring and lineage. And His saying:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[160] ﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah.﴾

﴿Except the sincere servants of Allah﴾ is an exception from "those who are brought forth" (al-muhdarin), namely the jinn. It is a connected exception (istithna' muttasil) according to the first opinion, meaning: the believers among them. It is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati') according to the second opinion, or an exception disconnected from the "wāw" in "yasifun" (they describe). Here remains an aspect of the verse that they have not mentioned: that "nasab" (lineage) is meant as kinship and affinity in worship and conformity in devotion, and that "al-jinna" is meant as the angels, so that the purpose of the verse is to inform about those among the Arabs who worshipped the angels and made them equals and likenesses to Him, exalted is He, and it is a report of another misguidance of theirs, other than the misguidance of their claim that they are the daughters of Allah, subhanahu, arising from their worship of them, despite the fact that the angels, peace be upon them, know that these misguided ones are brought forth to punishment. The verse in this regard is like the verse: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these people used to worship you?"﴾ [Saba': 40] ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our Guardian, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾ [Saba': 41]. The context from here to the end, like the context at the beginning of the surah, is entirely about affirming the servitude of the angels to Him, exalted is He, and that they are among His creatures who stand in rows for His worship. So how could they deserve lordship? And Allah knows best. And His saying:

(p-5068) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[161] ﴿So indeed you, and what you worship﴾.

﴿So indeed you, and what you worship﴾ is a return to addressing them.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[162] ﴿Indeed, you cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him,﴾

﴿You cannot lead astray [anyone] against Him,﴾ i.e., you cannot corrupt anyone through misguidance.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying:

[163] ﴿Except him who is to burn in the Hellfire.﴾

﴿Except him who is to burn in the Hellfire.﴾ That is: astray like you, deserving of the Fire. Ibn Jarir said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed you, O polytheists, in God, ﴿and what you worship﴾ [al-Saffat: 161] of the gods and idols, ﴿you cannot tempt [anyone] against Him﴾ [al-Saffat: 162], that is: you are not, with what you worship besides God, able to lead anyone astray, ﴿except him who is to burn in the Hellfire﴾, that is: whoever has preceded in My knowledge that he is to burn in the Hellfire. It has been said that the meaning of ʿalayhi is bihi [i.e., "with it"]. End of quote.

Then God explained the acknowledgment of the angels of servitude, in order to refute their worshippers, by His saying, relating from them:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted Saying:

[164] ﴿There is none of us but that he has a known station.﴾

﴿There is none of us but that he has a known station.﴾ That is: in servitude (ʿubudiyyah) and in being subjected (taskhīr) to what He, Exalted is He, wills from him. He does not transgress his own bound in it, nor exceed from it his measure.

(p-٥٠٦٩) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[ 165 ] ﴿And indeed, it is We who are the ones standing in ranks.﴾

﴿And indeed, it is We who are the ones standing in ranks.﴾ That is: in the performance of obedience, and in the stations of service to which we are commanded.

The commentary on His saying, may He be exalted:

[166] ﴿And indeed, we are they who glorify (Him)﴾.

﴿And indeed, we are they who glorify (Him)﴾, that is: those who declare God far above what the unbelievers ascribe to Him, or those who pray to Him in humility before His greatness and in lowliness before His majesty.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[167] ﴿And indeed they used to say﴾.

﴿And indeed they used to say﴾ i.e., the polytheists of Quraysh.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[168] ﴿Had we had a reminder from the former peoples﴾.

﴿Had we had a reminder from the former peoples﴾: that is, a Book from among the books that were revealed to them.

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted, verse:

[169] ﴿Indeed, we would have been sincere servants of Allah.﴾

﴿Indeed, we would have been sincere servants of Allah.﴾ That is: we would have made worship purely for Him. Then there came to them the Reminder (al-dhikr), which is the lord of reminders, and the Book (al-kitab), which is the most guiding of books and the most miraculous among them.

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[170] ﴿So they disbelieved in it, but they will come to know.﴾

(p-5070) ﴿So they disbelieved in it, but they will come to know.﴾ That is: the consequence of their disbelief. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the [other] nations. But when a warner came to them, it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ [Fatir: 42], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lest you say, "The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and we were indeed unaware of what they studied"﴾ [al-An'am: 156], and ﴿Or lest you say, "If the Book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than them." But there has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy. So who is more wrong than one who denies the signs of God and turns away from them?﴾ [al-An'am: 157].

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[171] ﴿And indeed Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers.﴾

﴿And indeed Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers.﴾ That is: Our eternal promise to them, which is:

[172, 173] ﴿Indeed, they will surely be given victory﴾ ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers, they will surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173].

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they will surely be given victory﴾ ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers﴾ [al-Saffat: 173], meaning: the Messengers and those who believed with them. ﴿They will surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173], meaning: those who prevail over their enemies and who hold their forelocks (i.e., have mastery over them), like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿God has decreed, "Surely I and My Messengers will prevail." Indeed, God is Powerful and Mighty﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21].

[172, 173] ﴿Indeed, they will surely be given victory﴾ ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers, they will surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173].

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they will surely be given victory﴾ ﴿And indeed, Our soldiers﴾ [al-Saffat: 173], meaning: the Messengers and those who believed with them. ﴿They will surely be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173], meaning: those who prevail over their enemies and who hold their forelocks (i.e., have mastery over them), like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿God has decreed, "Surely I and My Messengers will prevail." Indeed, God is Powerful and Mighty﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21].

The commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[174] ﴿So turn away from them for a time.﴾

﴿So turn away from them﴾ means: turn away from them with the turning away of one who pardons and forbears toward someone who harms him. Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And leave off harming them﴾ [al-Ahzab: 48], and His saying: ﴿So pardon with gracious pardon﴾ [al-Hijr: 85]. ﴿For a time﴾ means: until the victory is established for you.

The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[175] ﴿And see them, and they will [soon] see.﴾

﴿And see them﴾, i.e., make them see, and make them aware of the outcome of rebellion (al-baghy) and disbelief (al-kufr), and of what befell those who were warned before them. Or: make the proofs and arguments clear to them in your striving against them through the Qur'an and the revelation. If they do not see now, ﴿then they will soon see﴾, i.e., [they will see] what We have decreed for you of support (al-ta'yid) and victory (al-nusrah).

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 37, verse 176:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[176] ﴿Then is it Our punishment that they seek to hasten?﴾

﴿Then is it Our punishment that they seek to hasten?﴾ That is: before the arrival of its appointed time. And it is certainly coming, for it is the Day of Victory that was promised.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[177] ﴿So when it descends upon their courtyard, evil will be the morning of those who were warned.﴾

﴿When it descends upon their courtyard﴾ means: near them and in their open space. ﴿Evil will be the morning of those who were warned﴾ means: how wretched is the morning for those whom We warned through the messengers but who did not believe, for it is the day of their destruction and ruin. Al-Zamakhshari said: He likened the punishment that descended upon them, after they had been warned and had denied it, to an army whose attack one of their sincere advisers had warned of, yet they did not heed his warning, nor did they take up their arms or plan their affairs in a way that would save them, until it halted in their open space suddenly, launched its raid upon them, and cut off their last trace. Their raiders were accustomed to attacking at dawn, so the raid was called (morning), even if it occurred at another time. This verse would not have been eloquent, nor would it have had the awe that you feel and the delight its source brings to you and your nature, except for its coming in the manner of a figurative representation (tamthil). End of quotation. That is: it is a metaphor of the representative type (istiʿara tamthiliyya), or, in the pronoun there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿara makniyya), and the descending is imaginative (takhyiliyya).

(p-٥٠٧٢) The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[178, 179] ﴿So turn away from them for a while.﴾ ﴿And watch, for they will see.﴾ [al-Saffat: 179]

﴿So turn away from them for a while.﴾ ﴿And watch, for they will see.﴾ [al-Saffat: 179] Al-Zamakhshari said: He only repeated that as a consolation upon a consolation, and as an emphasis on the certainty of the appointed time upon emphasis. There is in it an additional benefit: the two verbs are released together from being restricted to an object, so that He sees and they see what cannot be encompassed by mention, of the kinds of joy and the varieties of harm. It was said: by one of them is meant the punishment of this world, and by the other, the punishment of the Hereafter.

(p-٥٠٧٢) The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[178, 179] ﴿So turn away from them for a while.﴾ ﴿And watch, for they will see.﴾ [al-Saffat: 179]

﴿So turn away from them for a while.﴾ ﴿And watch, for they will see.﴾ [al-Saffat: 179] Al-Zamakhshari said: He only repeated that as a consolation upon a consolation, and as an emphasis on the certainty of the appointed time upon emphasis. There is in it an additional benefit: the two verbs are released together from being restricted to an object, so that He sees and they see what cannot be encompassed by mention, of the kinds of joy and the varieties of harm. It was said: by one of them is meant the punishment of this world, and by the other, the punishment of the Hereafter.

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

[180] ﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe.﴾

﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of might﴾: i.e., of invincibility, power, and dominance. ﴿Above what they describe﴾: i.e., of partners, offspring, and the like.

The commentary on the words of God, Exalted is He:

[181] ﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾.

﴿And peace be upon the messengers﴾: that is, peace, and security, and greeting upon the messengers who conveyed the messages of their Lord.

Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted:

[182] ﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ — i.e., for His blessings, the greatest of which is the sending of the Messengers to manifest His Most Beautiful Names and His exalted laws, and to set right the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

(p-5073) Benefits concerning the conclusion of this surah:

The First: Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Walid ibn Abd Allah, who said: "They used not to line up in rows in prayer until the verse was revealed: ﴿And indeed, we are those who line up﴾ [al-Saffat: 165], and then they lined up."

Abu Nadrah said: When the prayer was called, ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) would turn to the people with his face and say: "Straighten your rows, stand straight, for Allah wishes to guide you by the guidance of the angels." Then he would recite: ﴿And indeed, we are those who line up﴾ [al-Saffat: 165], and say: "Step back, so-and-so; step forward, so-and-so." Then he would step forward and say the takbir. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

In Sahih Muslim, from Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have been favoured over the people in three ways: our rows have been made like the rows of the angels, the earth has been made a place of prayer for us, and its dust has been made a means of purification for us."

The Second: al-Shaykhan narrated from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attacked Khaybar at dawn. When they came out with their axes and their spades and saw the army, they turned back saying: 'Muhammad, by Allah! Muhammad and the army!' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Allahu Akbar! Khaybar is ruined. When we arrive in the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned.'" His (ﷺ) quoting of the verse indicates that it encompasses the punishment of this world, primarily and directly.

The Third: Ibn Kathir said: Since glorification (tasbih) includes declaring Allah free of imperfection and clearing Him of deficiency by direct implication, and entails affirming perfection, just as praise (hamd) indicates affirming absolute attributes of perfection by direct implication and entails declaring Him free of deficiency, He joined them together in this place and in many places in the Qur'an. For this reason, the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Glory be to your Lord﴾ [al-Saffat: 180] and the verses that follow.

(p-5074) The Fourth: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Sha'bi, as a mursal report: "Whoever would like to be given the fullest measure of reward on the Day of Resurrection, let him say at the end of his sitting, when he wishes to rise: ﴿Glory be to your Lord﴾ [al-Saffat: 180] — and the verses that follow —."

It is also narrated from Ali as a mawquf report.

Al-Tabarani narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam as a marfu' report: "Whoever says after every prayer: ﴿Glory be to your Lord﴾ [al-Saffat: 180] and the verses that follow, three times, has taken the fullest measure of reward."

Al-Razi has explained that the conclusion of this noble surah comprises all the lofty subjects. Refer to him.
